newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products rise - gasoline up on firmer U.S.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products rise - gasoline up on firmer U.S.

text.p: Med oil products were mostly firmer on Wednesday, traders said.
Naphtha was up on expected demand from Asia. Arb trade was not thought workable at the close of Asian business, but likely to open. Supportive swaps buying by certain traders also helped.
Gasoline numbers were notionally firmer in the wake of stronger prices in the U.S., which were prompted by bullish weekly inventory data.
Gas oil demand was healthy following recent refinery run cuts in Italy and limited Russian supplies. But action was limited and traders said demand had not increased noticeably.
Sellers were moving numbers up on growing tightness but levels were notionally up just in line with gas oil futures.
Most refiners had only small jet parcels to offer and buyers took fright at current high freight rates. Brokers said putting together combination cargoes was proving very difficult.
Larger cargoes were on offer but at a price. Algerian and Greek sellers were holding off in the double figures. Internal Greek demand saw deals done at quotes high +$10-12 a tonne.
High sulphur cracked cargoes were unchanged around the $81 fob mark with the low avails matched by lack of demand. Only one major was heard offering bunker spec at high fob +$5 but no buyers seen.
A second trader said Russian avails continue to be scarce, adding :"The Black Sea is quiet dead these days."

Traders were sceptical over a deal for bunker spec on Tuesday at $95 cif Las Palmas, with some saying the price was too high. But the seller said it would come to about that level, with its good quality material factored in.
One percent was a little stronger with a buyer heard to have picked up a 45,000 tonne cargo at $102.35 cif in the north, after an earlier deal this week a touch lower.
